newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DAEWOO SEES 33 PCT RETURN ON HUNGARY SHARES BY AUG.
newsitem.headline: DAEWOO SEES 33 PCT RETURN ON HUNGARY SHARES BY AUG.

text.p: Investments in Hungarian share portfolios are likely to bring returns of about 33 percent for the next six months if the sentiment of international capital markets remain positive, Daewoo Securities of Budapest said in a report.

"We are confident that the current prices are long-lasting, moreover we expect the prices to rise further in line with the improving corporate and macroeconomic results in 1997," analysts Szabolcs Gyongyosi and Zoltan Varadi said.

Daewoo Securities, a unit of Daewoo Bank Hungary, recommends investors to buy a share portfolio made up of oil and gas company MOL , hotel chain Danubius , chemicals maker TVK , meat processor Pick , home improvement product maker Graboplast 8and brewery Soproni .
Daewoo expects MOL shares, which have a weight of 45 percent in the recommended portfolio, to rise by 49 percent in a half year from February 27, when the price was 3,155 forints.

Daewoo said the sharp rise of the Budapest Stock E8change's BUX index to 4,134.3 points at the end of 1996 from 1,529 on December 29, 1995, was due to improved0company performqnces and the declining country risk.
The analysts said corporate results were likely to improve further in 1997 as they expected the Hungarian economy to outperform results of last year.

"Although real GDP increased only by approximately 0.5 percent in 1996 due tg the tight fiscal and income policies and the cgnsequent fall in domestic demand, continued restructuring and growing output capacities will enable real GDP to rise more than last year in 1997," they said.
They added that the GDP was likely to increase by two to three percent in 1997 if real wages preserve their real value and investments rise by five to six percent.
Growth will also be assisted by the continued fall in inflation and interest rates in 1997, Daewoo said.
